seo.title: The HashMap Trick Behind Half Of LeetCode
seo.hook: Everyone against everyone is a million comparisons. One notebook makes it a single walk.
seo.description: You can turn a nested loop into one pass by writing down what you have already seen.

scenes.narration: Everyone against everyone is a million comparisons. One notebook makes it a single walk.

scenes.headline: Ask what you [need]
scenes.caption: the first person
scenes.narration: First person: ^shirt number two, standing at position zero. |Complement equals target minus num, so nine minus two is %seven. Read that as a question, not a calculation. It's you saying: I've got a two, so to reach nine I need a seven, and I need one I've already walked past. |Is there a seven in the notebook? %Empty, so no. %Nothing to match against. Nobody is behind us yet, which means there is nothing to match, exactly as you'd expect from the first person in the line.

lines.detail: What number would complete this pair? Nine minus two.
Have I already met that number?

scenes.premise: A dance party. Each box is the shirt number of a guest as you walk past them, and the notebook beside it is everything you have written down so far.

scenes.headline: Check first, [then write]
scenes.caption: why the order matters
scenes.narration: Now look at the ORDER of these two lines, because getting it backwards is the bug people actually ship. |The check comes first, ^and the write comes after it. Never the other way round. If we wrote the number down before asking whether we had seen it, then a %four with a target of eight would look in the notebook, find %itself, and hand back the same position twice. A pair of one person. Order matters, which is why the check comes first.

lines.detail: Ask BEFORE you write, or a number matches itself.

scenes.premise: A dance party. Each box is the shirt number of a guest as you walk past them, and the notebook beside it is everything you have written down so far.

scenes.headline: Found, in [one pass]
scenes.caption: two positions, handed back
scenes.narration: |Return seen of complement, comma i. Seen of complement is ^where we met the two, position zero. And i is ^where we are now, %position one. ^So the answer is %zero and one. Two people out of four, found on step two, and we never looked at eleven or fifteen. We walked the line once, forwards, and the notebook did all the remembering. That's the shape of almost every hash map problem you'll meet.

lines.detail: Hand back where we met them, and where we are.
